candidates.proposed_modification: Replace the implant-abutment connection with a Morse taper (conical) connection.
candidates.mechanistic_reasoning: The documented failure is screw loosening due to insufficient preload retention under masticatory forces. This geometry inherently resists rotational and axial displacement, reducing reliance on screw preload alone. Additionally, Morse taper systems demonstrate diameter-independent mechanical stability and prosthetic-controlled failure patterns, unlike internal hex systems, which are sensitive to diameter reduction and bone loss.
candidates.expected_effect: The modification will reduce the incidence of screw loosening by improving the stability of the implant-abutment interface, thereby maintaining long-term preload under functional loads.

candidates.why_different_from_baseline: The baseline (glutaraldehyde-fixed valves) lacks active anti-calcification, pro-endothelialization, and antifouling mechanisms. The proposed modification adds a functional bioactive coating (EGCG/Cu²⁺ MPN + zwitterionic polymer) that targets the root causes of calcification.
